methods.label: Find and adjust the daily pair price
methods.explanation:
Two weeks contain \(14\) days. Since Al takes one pill of each color daily, one green pill and one pink pill together cost
\[
\frac{546}{14}=39\text{ dollars}.
\]
A green pill costs one dollar more than a pink pill. Replacing the pink pill in this pair with another green pill therefore raises the cost to \(39+1=40\) dollars. Two green pills cost \(40\) dollars, so one costs \(\boxed{\$20}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses elementary total-price relationships and integer arithmetic.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task-level target is recovering unit prices from total price, quantity, and a price difference. The method divides to find the daily pair price and adjusts that sum to obtain two equal prices. Equation-modeling nodes are unnecessary for this arithmetic route.
